title: Beni Mellal city and foothills on 21 Aug 2026
summary: On 21 Aug 2026 the radar shows Beni Mellal city and its foothills inside a 6 km circle, with built-up land on 12.2% and trees, shrub and rugged slopes on 52.5%. No flag applies to this date.

sections.heading: What the radar shows here
sections.text: Built-up land reaches 6.07 dB in HH, far above the circle mean of -1.84 dB. HV averages -13.78 dB over the circle, and built-up land sits at -10.82 dB in HV.

sections.heading: Terrain types and what they mean
sections.text: Built-up land, 13.75 km2, has the lowest HV:HH ratio, -16.89 dB, the double-bounce signature of walls. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes, 59.32 km2, give HV of -12.87 dB from volume scattering. Rough dry ground and fields, 30.89 km2, sit at -10.55 dB in HH. Changing fields cover 5.4 km2 at -17.41 dB in HV, the darkest HV of the field types on this date apart from smooth bare ground at -22.2 dB.

sections.heading: Data quality notes
sections.text: No flag applies. One track only, so slopes facing away from the radar can fall in shadow. Possible cause of the dark HV on changing fields: harvested or bare plots at the end of summer; the optical photo or a field visit would check it.
